# PLAYBOOK.md

How the `spoke` team works with Claude Code. Every line here points at something the repo
already holds: `work/approvals.jsonl`, `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

## Our AI stance

Claude drafts the work. A person in a named role signs the files that gate it. A sign-off is a
line in `work/approvals.jsonl` that records the file's `sha256`, the approver's role, their name
and the time, so each sign-off covers that exact version of the file.

## Gates

| File                                    | Who approves    | How it is recorded                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `work/intent.md`                        | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/spec.md`                          | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/plan.md`                          | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `test/acceptance`                       | qa              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `REVIEW.md`                             | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/release.md`                       | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/rollout.yaml`                     | release-manager | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/postmortem.md`                    | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md`   | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |

`work/spec.md` and `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` were each signed twice. The latest
line is the one that counts.

## Never do

- `Edit(/data/contract/**)`: denied. Claude cannot edit the city contract (`data/contract/sla.yaml`).
- `Write(/data/contract/**)`: denied. Claude cannot write files under `data/contract/`.
- `Bash(bun run deploy:production *)`: ask. A person must say yes before Claude can run it.

## Size of a change

`CLAUDE.md` does not set a limit on changed lines. `work/plan.md` sets a target for the current
feature only: P-2 to P-5 each go in their own commit, and each stays under 200 changed lines.
That target is not a rule for the whole repo.

## When we use the factory

Nothing in the repo sets up runs with no person in the loop, and no kind of change is marked as
safe to run that way. So no change may run unattended yet.

These may never run without a person:

- Edits or writes to `data/contract/**`. They are denied outright.
- `bun run deploy:production`. It is an ask rule, so it waits for a person's yes.
- Any file in the Gates table. Each one needs a sign-off from the role listed there.

How the `spoke` team works with Claude Code. Everything here is backed by a file already in the
repo: `work/approvals.jsonl`, `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.

## Our AI stance

Claude drafts the work; people sign off on it. Each gated file needs a sign-off from a person in
a named role. A sign-off is one line in `work/approvals.jsonl` that records the file's `sha256`,
the approver's role (`role`), their name (`by`) and the time (`at`). Because the line pins the
hash, a sign-off covers only that exact version of the file: change the file and it needs signing
again.

## Gates

Each file below needs a sign-off from the listed role, recorded as a line in
`work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by` and `at`.

| File                                     | Who approves    |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `work/intent.md`                         | pm              |
| `work/spec.md`                           | pm              |
| `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` | tech-lead       |
| `work/plan.md`                           | tech-lead       |
| `test/acceptance`                        | qa              |
| `REVIEW.md`                              | tech-lead       |
| `work/release.md`                        | pm              |
| `work/rollout.yaml`                      | release-manager |
| `work/postmortem.md`                     | tech-lead       |
| `work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md`    | pm              |

`work/spec.md` and `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` have each been signed twice. When a
file has more than one sign-off, the latest line is the one that counts.

## What Claude can't do on its own

These rules live in `.claude/settings.json`:

- `Edit(/data/contract/**)` is **denied**: Claude can't edit the city contract
  (`data/contract/sla.yaml`).
- `Write(/data/contract/**)` is **denied**: Claude can't create or overwrite files under
  `data/contract/`.
- `Bash(bun run deploy:production *)` is set to **ask**: Claude can run it only after a person
  says yes.

## Size of a change

`CLAUDE.md` sets no limit on how many lines a change can touch. `work/plan.md` sets a target for
the current feature only: steps P-2 to P-5 each go in their own commit, and each commit stays
under 200 changed lines. That target applies to this feature, not to the whole repo.

## When we use the factory (unattended runs)

The "factory" means letting Claude run with no person in the loop. Nothing in the repo sets that
up yet, and no kind of change is marked as safe for it. So for now, no change runs unattended.

Even once unattended runs exist, these will always need a person:

- Edits or writes to `data/contract/**`. They are denied outright.
- `bun run deploy:production`. It is an ask rule, so it waits for a person's yes.
- Any file in the Gates table. Each one needs a sign-off from the role listed there.

# PLAYBOOK.md

How the `spoke` team works with Claude Code. Everything here is backed by a file already in the
repo: `work/approvals.jsonl`, `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.

## Our AI stance

Claude drafts the work; people sign off on it. Each gated file needs a sign-off from a person in
a named role. A sign-off is one line in `work/approvals.jsonl` that records the file's `sha256`,
the approver's role (`role`), their name (`by`) and the time (`at`). Because the line pins the
hash, a sign-off covers only that exact version of the file: change the file and it needs signing
again.

## Gates

Each file below needs a sign-off from the listed role, recorded as a line in
`work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by` and `at`.

| File                                     | Who approves    |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `work/intent.md`                         | pm              |
| `work/spec.md`                           | pm              |
| `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` | tech-lead       |
| `work/plan.md`                           | tech-lead       |
| `test/acceptance`                        | qa              |
| `REVIEW.md`                              | tech-lead       |
| `work/release.md`                        | pm              |
| `work/rollout.yaml`                      | release-manager |
| `work/postmortem.md`                     | tech-lead       |
| `work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md`    | pm              |

`work/spec.md` and `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` have each been signed twice. When a
file has more than one sign-off, the latest line is the one that counts.

## What Claude can't do on its own

These rules live in `.claude/settings.json`:

- `Edit(/data/contract/**)` is **denied**: Claude can't edit the city contract
  (`data/contract/sla.yaml`).
- `Write(/data/contract/**)` is **denied**: Claude can't create or overwrite files under
  `data/contract/`.
- `Bash(bun run deploy:production *)` is set to **ask**: Claude can run it only after a person
  says yes.

## Size of a change

`CLAUDE.md` sets no limit on how many lines a change can touch. `work/plan.md` sets a target for
the current feature only: steps P-2 to P-5 each go in their own commit, and each commit stays
under 200 changed lines. That target applies to this feature, not to the whole repo.

## When we use the factory (unattended runs)

The "factory" means letting Claude run with no person in the loop. Nothing in the repo sets that
up yet, and no kind of change is marked as safe for it. So for now, no change runs unattended.

Even once unattended runs exist, these will always need a person:

- Edits or writes to `data/contract/**`. They are denied outright.
- `bun run deploy:production`. It is an ask rule, so it waits for a person's yes.
- Any file in the Gates table. Each one needs a sign-off from the role listed there.

I've reworded `PLAYBOOK.md` for new hires. The facts, rules, roles and file list are unchanged. I haven't committed it.

**This edit voids the current sign-off.** Dana Okafor (em) approved `PLAYBOOK.md` today, and that approval line in `work/approvals.jsonl` covers only the old version of the file (by its hash). The new version needs a fresh em sign-off before it counts. I didn't add an approval line myself, because only that person can. If you'd rather keep the signed version, `git checkout PLAYBOOK.md` puts it back.

What changed:
- **Gates table:** the "How it is recorded" column said the same thing on all ten rows. I replaced it with one sentence above the table, so the table now just lists each file and who approves it.
- **Our AI stance:** it now says outright that editing a signed file means it has to be signed again. The original only implied this.
- **"Never do" is now "What Claude can't do on its own":** the deploy rule asks for a person's yes rather than blocking outright, so the old heading was misleading. The section now says these rules live in `.claude/settings.json`, and the words "denied" and "ask" are in bold.
- **The factory section:** it now explains that "factory" means letting Claude run with no person in the loop, since new hires won't know the term.
- **Size of a change:** small clarifications, such as calling P-2 to P-5 "steps" and saying the 200-line target is per commit.
